candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is granuloma annulare, which is characterized by necrobiosis, mucin (Alcian-blue positive), and palisading/multinucleated giant cells — all present in this case. Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma (NXG) is a related but distinct granulomatous disorder that requires xanthomatous (foamy) histiocytes, cholesterol clefts, and is strongly associated with paraproteinemia/plasma cell dyscrasias. The candidate invokes NXG as the diagnosis, which is an incompatible subtype within the necrobiotic granuloma family. The histopathology described (necrobiosis, Alcian-blue positive mucin, giant cells, no xanthomatous features mentioned) and the periorbital post-surgical setting in the absence of systemic disease markers better fits granuloma annulare (particularly deep/subcutaneous type) rather than NXG.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma is a distinct clinicopathological entity from granuloma annulare; both share necrobiosis and mucin but differ in xanthomatous histology, lipid deposition, paraproteinemia association, and clinical context

case_quality_flags: Histopathology is consistent with deep granuloma annulare; NXG would require xanthomatous histiocytes and cholesterol clefts not described in the record
Periorbital location post-DCR with necrobiosis and mucin is a recognized presentation of deep/subcutaneous granuloma annulare
